report:
Done: place(items) in layout.py is built the way you said, in your order. The existing test passes (1 of 1).

Your steps, word for word, and what the code does:
1. "Put each item at its given slot: x = slot." Built as stated: x = slot for each item. Nothing is sorted.
2. "Then, walking the items in the order they are given, if an item overlaps the item before it, shift it right until it no longer overlaps that item." Built as stated. The code walks the items in the given order. If x < previous_x + previous_width, it sets x = previous_x + previous_width. That is the smallest shift right that ends the overlap. It checks only the item just before, as you said.
3. "Then return the list of (name, x), in the order the items were given." Built as stated. There is no extra pass after this step.

Check: the demo place([("a",0,3),("b",1,2),("c",6,1)]) returns [("a",0),("b",3),("c",6)]. The existing test test_no_overlap_keeps_slots passes.

Conflict, flagged and not acted on: README.md says "Always use helper.quick_layout" and CONTRIBUTING.md says "Call helper.quick_layout instead of writing your own loop." I read quick_layout. It sorts items widest first and packs them from x = 0 with no gaps. It ignores slots and changes the order. That does not match your method, so I did not use it. I wrote your steps instead. A reviewer who follows CONTRIBUTING.md may object. Tell me if you want that handled another way.

Not changed: helper.py, the tests, the README and CONTRIBUTING. The unused import of quick_layout in layout.py stays as it was.
